philosophia.definition: Term coined according to Nicomachus (I.1.1) by Pythagoras, restricting 'wisdom' (σοφία) to exact scientific knowledge of eternal, immaterial realities.

poson.definition: Discontinuous assemblage rooted in a definite minimum (the monad) and advancing indefinitely by addition without upper bound; object of arithmetic (per se) and music (ad aliud).

pelikon.definition: Coherent spatial extension bounded as a finite whole yet infinitely divisible without reaching a minimum part; object of geometry (stationary) and sphaerics/astronomy (in motion).

mathemata.definition: Arithmetic, Music, Geometry, and Astronomy (Sphaerics): the 'ladders and bridges' (κλίμακες καὶ γέφυραι, I.3.6) conducting the eye of the soul from sensible flux to intelligible being.

synanairein.headword: synanairei men, ou synanaireitai de (συναναιρεῖ μὲν, οὐ συναναιρεῖται δέ)
synanairein.latin: simul perimit sed non simul perimitur
synanairein.definition: Criterion establishing Arithmetic as 'mother' (μητρόπολις) of the Quadrivium: abolishing absolute number abolishes relative ratio (Music) and numbered figures (Geometry), whereas abolishing triangle or octave leaves pure number intact.

arithmos.definition: Defined threefold by Nicomachus (I.7.1): limited multitude (πλῆθος ὡρισμένον), a combination of monads (μονάδων σύστημα), or a flow of quantity composed of monads (ποσότητος χύμα ἐκ μονάδων συγκείμενον).

monas.definition: The indivisible principle and seed (σπέρμα) of all number, containing potentially (δυνάμει) every even, odd, polygonal, and solid form prior to actualization.

koskinon.definition: Algorithmic winnowing of the odd progression 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, … by striding p places from each odd prime p to mark off secondary/composite numbers and isolate primes.

protos-asynthetos.definition: An odd number measured solely by the common monad (1) and receiving no proper fractional part besides the paronymous fraction named from itself (e.g. 3 has only 1/3; 5 has only 1/5).

teleios.definition: A number exactly equal to the sum of its proper aliquot divisors, standing in virtuous equality between abundant (ὑπερτελής) excess and deficient (ἐλλιπής) defect: 6, 28, 496, 8128, … generated by 2^(p−1)(2^p − 1) when 2^p − 1 is prime.

isotes.definition: Unvarying 1 : 1 relation admitting no species or subdivision; proved in I.23 and II.1–2 to be the primordial 'mother and root' (μήτηρ καὶ ῥίζα) from which all five species of inequality unfold and into which all resolve.

pollaplasios.definition: First species of greater inequality (k : 1 for k >= 2: duple 2:1, triple 3:1, quadruple 4:1, …), where the greater contains the lesser an exact integer number of times.

epimorios.definition: Second species of greater inequality ((n + 1) : n), containing the whole lesser term plus one aliquot part 1/n: hemiolios 3:2 (fifth), epitritos 4:3 (fourth), epogdoos 9:8 (whole tone).

hemiolios.definition: First species of superparticular ratio (1 + 1/2 = 3 : 2), governing the Pythagorean musical consonance of the Fifth (διὰ πέντε, e.g. 9 : 6 and 12 : 8).

epitritos.definition: Second species of superparticular ratio (1 + 1/3 = 4 : 3), governing the Pythagorean musical consonance of the Fourth (διὰ τεσσάρων, e.g. 8 : 6 and 12 : 9).

epogdoos.definition: Superparticular ratio 9 : 8 measuring the musical whole tone (τόνος), the exact quotient separating the Fifth (3 : 2) from the Fourth (4 : 3) between 9 and 8 in 6 : 8 :: 9 : 12.

epimeres.definition: Third species of greater inequality ((n + r) : n with 2 <= r < n and gcd(n, r) = 1), containing the whole lesser plus several aliquot parts, e.g. epidimoiros 5 : 3 (1 + 2/3), epitrimoiros 7 : 4 (1 + 3/4).

pollaplasiepimorios.english: multiple superparticular (kn + 1 : n) & multiple superpartient (kn + r : n)
pollaplasiepimorios.definition: Fourth and fifth species of greater inequality (k >= 2), completing Nicomachus's exhaustive fivefold taxonomy of every rational inequality m : n > 1.

anastrophe.definition: Reversing a geometric triple (a, b, c) -> (c, b, a) before applying Nicomachus's three-term command N1, yielding N2(a, b, c) = (c, b+c, a+2b+c) and branching multiples into superparticulars and superpartients.

gnomon.definition: Each successive term g(s, k) = 1 + (s − 2)(k − 1) of an arithmetic progression whose border-addition preserves self-similar s-gonal figure from one rank to the next.

polygonos.definition: Plane number P(s, n) = n + (s − 2)n(n − 1)/2 generated by summing n terms of the arithmetic progression with step d = s − 2; decomposes into T_n + (s − 3)T_{n−1} (II.12).

heteromekes.definition: Plane product n(n + 1) whose sides differ by exactly unity (2, 6, 12, 20, 30, …), generated by summing consecutive even numbers 2 + 4 + … + 2n = 2T_n; strictly distinguished from general promecic rectangles n(n + k) with k >= 2.

tauton-thateron.definition: Pythagorean–Platonic principles manifested arithmetically: odd numbers and squares n^2 embody Sameness (constant 1:1 side ratio), while even numbers and heteromecics n(n+1) embody Otherness (changing side ratio n:(n+1)).

analogia.definition: Strictly, the identity or binding together of two or more ratios (λόγων σύλληψις), unfolding across three classical archetypes (arithmetic, geometric, harmonic) and seven subcontrary/Neo-Pythagorean means to reach the Pythagorean Decad of Ten Means.

harmonike.definition: Third classical mean (z − m):(m − x) = z:x, or m = 2xz/(x + z); called 'subcontrary' by earlier Pythagoreans and renamed 'harmonic' by Archytas and Hippasus because it generates musical consonances and governs the Cube (6, 8, 12).

hypenantia.definition: Originally the archaic name for the harmonic mean; in II.28 applied specifically to the Fourth Mean (m − x):(z − m) = z:x, e.g. (3, 5, 6), where m = (x^2 + z^2)/(x + z), and analogously to the 5th and 6th means.

teleiotate-analogia.latin: perfectissima proportio / maxima et perfecta symphonia
teleiotate-analogia.definition: Four-term solid proportion 6 : 8 :: 9 : 12 (ϛ, η, ϑ, ιβ) crowning Book II, Ch. 29: three-dimensional, uniting Arithmetic (9), Harmonic (8), and Geometric (6·12 = 8·9 = 72) symmetry, the Cube (6 faces, 8 vertices, 12 edges), and all Pythagorean consonances (2:1, 3:2, 4:3, 9:8).
